object_description: bent multi-storey building complex forming an urban front
design_condition: The new complex occupies the convergence of two urban fabrics, defines street edges, bends toward the public square, and uses a setback to moderate its scale in the historic surroundings.

positive.statement: The new volume makes a significant urban-development contribution, defines clear street boundaries, and strongly connects to the public square.

position.rationale: The bent large-volume footprint and continuous elevations visibly define an urban front.

positive.statement: The bent façade acts as an invitation to public space and restores an urban front.

position.rationale: The broad northern bend forms the visible edge facing the open side of the plan.

positive.statement: The setback softens the building’s scale and approaches the small-scale proportions and heights of the historic fabric.

position.rationale: The stepped eastern side visibly recedes within the bent footprint and tall elevations.

positive.statement: The new spacious areas can react flexibly to changing uses.

position.rationale: Interior flexibility is unshown; the anchor occupies a broad central zone within the sampled complex.

positive.statement: The operational concept is interesting and would work.

position.rationale: Operational performance is assessed globally without a specific geometric referent.

negative.statement: The central access core is obscured by the differing heights between the existing and new buildings.

position.rationale: The central bend suggests the access interface, though no core is explicitly distinguishable.

negative.statement: The interface between the buildings is unconvincing because the new volume rises substantially above the existing eaves.

position.target: interface between existing and new buildings
position.rationale: The interface is approximated along the upper-left junction of the bent sampled masses.

negative.statement: The intervention is not sufficiently sensitive to the protected old building and isolates its central staircase from natural light and new relationships.

position.target: protected old building and central staircase
position.rationale: Existing fabric and staircase are not distinguishable; the marker uses the western lower mass.

negative.statement: The height development is hardly compatible with the urban context and the market-square setting.

position.rationale: Dense elevations clearly show substantial multi-storey height across the bent complex.

negative.statement: The expected construction costs are significantly above average.

position.rationale: Cost is a non-spatial judgment without a model location.
